Accessed September 4, 2014. | website = {{URL|redbanknj.org}} | footnotes = }} '''Red Bank''' is a [[Borough (New Jersey)|borough]] in [[Monmouth County, New Jersey|Monmouth County]], in the [[U.S. state]] of [[New Jersey]]. Incorporated in 1908, the community is on the [[Navesink River]], the area's original transportation route to the [[Atlantic Ocean]] and to other [[port]]s. Red Bank is in the [[New York metropolitan area]] and is a [[commuter town]] of [[New York City]].Capuzzo, Jill P. [https://www.nytimes.com/2016/07/17/realestate/red-bank-the-jersey-shore-with-an-urban-vibe.html "Living In Red Bank: The Jersey Shore With an Urban Vibe’"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', July 13, 2016, Accessed June 14, 2022. As of the [[2020 United States census]], the borough's population was 12,936, its highest decennial census count ever and an increase of 730 (+6.0%) from the [[2010 United States census|2010 census]] count of 12,206, which in turn had reflected an increase of 362 (+3.1%) from the 11,844 counted at the [[2000 United States census|2000 census]].[https://www.nj.gov/labor/labormarketinformation/assets/PDFs/census/2010/2010data/table7cm.xls Table 7. Population for the Counties and Municipalities in New Jersey: 1990, 2000 and 2010], [[New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development]], February 2011. Accessed May 1, 2023. In the 2020 census, Red Bank was the fourth-most densely populated municipality in Monmouth County. Red Bank was formed as a [[Town (New Jersey)|town]] on March 17, 1870, from parts of [[Shrewsbury Township, New Jersey|Shrewsbury Township]]. On February 14, 1879, Red Bank became Shrewsbury City, part of Shrewsbury Township; this lasted until May 15, 1879, when Red Bank regained its independence. On March 10, 1908, Red Bank was formed as a borough by an act of the [[New Jersey Legislature]] and was set off from Shrewsbury Township.Snyder, John P. [https://nj.gov/dep/njgs/enviroed/oldpubs/bulletin67.pdf ''The Story of New Jersey's Civil Boundaries: 1606-1968''], Bureau of Geology and Topography; Trenton, New Jersey; 1969. p. 184. Accessed May 30, 2024.Honeyman, Abraham Van Doren. [https://books.google.com/books?id=nOkkAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA230 ''Index-analysis of the Statutes of New Jersey, 1896-1909: Together with References to All Acts, and Parts of Acts, in the 'General Statutes' and Pamphlet Laws Expressly Repealed: and the Statutory Crimes of New Jersey During the Same Period''], p. 230. New Jersey Law Journal Publishing Company, 1910. Accessed September 22, 2015. The borough was named for the red soil along the Navesink River.Hutchinson, Viola L. [http://mapmaker.rutgers.edu/356/nj_place_names_origin.pdf#page=27 ''The Origin of New Jersey Place Names''], New Jersey Public Library Commission, May 1945. Accessed September 21, 2015.[[Henry Gannett|Gannett, Henry]]. [https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_9V1IAAAAMAAJ/page/n258 ''The Origin of Certain Place Names in the United States''], p. 259. [[United States Government Printing Office]], 1905. Accessed September 21, 2015. Downtown Red Bank is notable for its many local and well-known businesses including Garmany, [[Urban Outfitters]], and [[Tiffany & Co.]]{{Cite web|title=Shopping in Red Bank|url=https://www.redbank.org/directory/shopping/all/|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.redbank.org}} on and around Broad Street. Many annual events happen throughout the year, including the International Beer, Wine & Food Festival,{{Cite web|title=Annual Red Bank INTERNATIONAL BEER, WINE & FOOD FESTIVAL|url=http://www.rueevents.com/information_31.html|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.rueevents.com}} a long-running sidewalk sale,{{Cite web|title=Events {{!}} Red Bank Sidewalk Sale|url=https://www.redbank.org/events/97/67th-annual-red-bank-sidewalk-sale/|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.redbank.org}} a [[farmers' market]],{{Cite web|title=Events {{!}} Red Bank Farmers Market|url=https://www.redbank.org/events/91/red-bank-farmers-market-2021/|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.redbank.org}} an [[Independent film|indie]] [[film festival]],{{Cite web|title=Home {{!}} Indie Street Film Festival|url=https://www.indiestreetfilmfestival.org/#about|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.indiestreetfilmfestival.org}} the Red Bank [[Guinness]] [[Oyster festival|Oyster Festival]],{{Cite web|title=Guinness Oyster Festival|url=http://www.rueevents.com/information_10.html|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.rueevents.com}} a Halloween parade,{{Cite web|title=Events {{!}} Red Bank Halloween Parade|url=https://www.redbank.org/events/40/halloween-parade/|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.redbank.org}} and a holiday town lighting.{{Cite web|title=Events {{!}} Red Bank Holiday Lighting|url=https://www.redbank.org/events/99/29th-annual-town-lighting-holiday-express-concert-2021/|access-date=2021-11-23|website=www.redbank.org}}
